executive_summary.headline: Proactive agents are the week's creator story
executive_summary.body: Anthropic opened a waitlist for Claude Duet on October 21 and creators posted explainers within hours, at least ten on Instagram alone. Allie K. Miller's LinkedIn tests put Duet next to Muse, Dots and Instinct, and her advice is to write down what may interrupt you before connecting any of them.

executive_summary.headline: Your own past work is the best prompt
executive_summary.body: Andrew Bailiff turned two years of his client reports into a style file and now runs his weekly report from it. Easter Gay Maanao reports a 10-minute audit that used to take over an hour, and Helium 10 lets sellers write ad rules in sentences.

executive_summary.headline: Meta says agents are buying, and Anthropic shows a nonexpert group getting wet-lab results
executive_summary.body: Meta says over 10 million people set up Muse agents and the average purchase tops $200. Anthropic says Claude designed 211 scorpion-toxin binders in 64 hours and 17 passed lab tests, in a project steered by a nonexpert investment research group.

top_picks.title: Claude Duet launches and creators turn it into a same-day Reel wave
top_picks.summary: Claude Duet is a proactive agent that messages you first, reads email and calendar, checks in every 3 hours and runs on its own cloud machine. A creator's explainer Reel reached 3,596 likes and 43 comments a day after Anthropic opened the waitlist for US Pro and Max subscribers on October 21.
top_picks.author: @vaibhavsisinty
top_picks.enterprise_translation: Steal the morning-brief pattern: an assistant that opens your day with the three things that need you and stays quiet otherwise. Fake it this week by asking any chatbot to turn your inbox and calendar into a five-line brief at 8am, then keep the format that you actually read.
top_picks.category: New capability / consumer and small business
top_picks.why_it_matters: Anthropic positions Duet for professionals and small business owners, and it shows how fast a launch becomes creator content.

top_picks.title: Allie K. Miller matches Muse, Dots and Instinct to the person who should use each
top_picks.summary: Miller's side-by-side calls Muse best for heavy Instagram and Facebook users and as an idea generator, Dots best for OpenAI users who code or live in Slack, and Instinct best for people who live in iMessage. The post drew 201 reactions and 167 comments.
top_picks.author: Allie K. Miller
top_picks.enterprise_translation: Pick an assistant by persona instead of by benchmark. Hand three colleagues or family members a different agent for one week and compare which one each person actually opens on day five.
top_picks.recurrence_note: Muse was a Top Pick last week; this week it is compared against two new rivals.

top_picks.title: Allie K. Miller: write three rules before you connect a proactive agent
top_picks.summary: Miller tested Claude Duet against Instinct, Muse, Grokbot, Tab, OpenAI dots and Hermes. She says the skill has shifted from asking good questions to deciding what is allowed to interrupt you, and that Duet was the most proactive of the group. The post drew 281 reactions and 199 comments.
top_picks.author: Allie K. Miller
top_picks.enterprise_translation: A one-page autonomy brief travels with you to any assistant: what counts as urgent this month, what it may do alone, what needs your OK. Write yours in ten minutes and paste it into the first assistant you try.

top_picks.title: Claude designs scorpion-toxin binders in 64 hours; 17 of 211 tested designs hold up in the lab
top_picks.summary: Anthropic's Instagram post says an internal research model working inside Claude Science designed minibinders against scorpion neurotoxins, with four follow-up prompts developed with Citrini Research, a group of motivated nonexperts. Adaptyv Bio and Twist Bioscience tested 211 designs and 17 met the criteria; Anthropic is releasing all 211 designs.
top_picks.author: @claudeai (Anthropic)
top_picks.enterprise_translation: A bounded, named challenge beats an open-ended AI mandate: one target, one 64-hour run, a wet-lab readout. Give a skeptical scientist group a single narrow problem from their own backlog, a two-day agent run, and a bench test of the top candidates.
top_picks.why_it_matters: Science bonus applied: AI-led protein design with experimental validation, and a nonexpert group driving it.

top_picks.title: Andrew Bailiff builds a style file from two years of his own client reports
top_picks.summary: Bailiff fed Claude two years of weekly client emails and meeting transcripts, had it write down how he leads, how short he keeps things and which metrics he repeats, then ran his weekly report off that file with numbers pulled through an MCP connection. The post has 20 reactions and 9 comments.
top_picks.author: Andrew Bailiff
top_picks.enterprise_translation: Context beats clever prompts: your past work is the best instruction set you own. Pull your last ten sent status reports, ask Claude what they share, save that as a style file, and attach it to next Friday's update.

top_picks.title: Meta says 10 million people set up Muse agents and shopping is the top use
top_picks.summary: On Meta's October 21 earnings call, Zuckerberg said more than 10 million US and Canadian users have set up Muse agents since September 8, a quarter of them use it daily, and the average purchase is over $200. Meta had to work with Stripe to raise credit limits in week one and plans to charge businesses a fee when Muse completes a sale.
top_picks.author: Meta / TechCrunch
top_picks.enterprise_translation: Consumers are already handing agents a credit card, which makes agent-completed sales a channel. List your five most-searched products and see which would survive being bought by an assistant with only a title, price and review score.
top_picks.recurrence_note: Muse was last week's Muse Wonder and ideas-tab story; this week adds adoption and revenue numbers.
top_picks.why_it_matters: Adoption figures come from the company's own earnings call and are relayed by TechCrunch and Fortune.

top_picks.title: YouTube creator Gossip Goblin lands a theatrical release for an AI-made animated feature
top_picks.summary: AGC International picked up 'Gods Don't Give Gifts' by Zack London, who posts as Gossip Goblin, for the American Film Market. Variety reports the trailer passed 15 million views since October 6 and AGC says the film opens in the US on December 4 as the first AI film with a traditional theatrical rollout and awards campaign.
top_picks.author: Zack London (Gossip Goblin)
top_picks.enterprise_translation: A single creator with a trailer-first release can pull in a sales agent and a theater run. Cut a 60-second trailer for a product story you have never had budget to film, post it, and see who asks for the full version.

secondary_urls.label: Trailer view count as reported by Variety

sections.title: LinkedIn
sections.description: Posts from AI voices and practitioners on LinkedIn this week, with reactions and comments as observed on the post pages.

items.title: Allie K. Miller: stop prompting, stop typing, stop using a computer screen
items.summary: Miller's three-line weekend challenge pushes people toward voice, ambient and agent-first use instead of typed prompts. It drew 485 reactions and 148 comments, the most of her posts this week.
items.author: Allie K. Miller
items.enterprise_translation: Run a no-keyboard weekend: dictate every AI request and let one agent handle a recurring chore without you opening a screen. Note which task you never went back to typing.

items.title: Ulta Beauty launches AI Bundles inside ChatGPT
items.summary: A retail executive announces the Ulta Beauty plugin in ChatGPT: shoppers share goals and budget, AI builds a bundle in real time with 10% off qualifying bundles, and the cart transfers to Ulta to check out. The post has 359 reactions and 25 comments.
items.author: Agustina Sartori
items.enterprise_translation: A bundle builder is a conversation that ends in a basket. Prototype one for your most configurable product line: a chat that takes a goal and a budget and returns a kit with a discount.

items.title: Rose Mwangi coaches a five-agent squad through the AWS Agentic Football Cup
items.summary: A hackathon builder ran five AI agents on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore with Claude Sonnet 4.6, watched them learn from mistakes to win a match, and used CloudWatch logs to see why each action happened. The post has 6 reactions and 1 comment.
items.author: Rose Mwangi
items.enterprise_translation: Games make agent behavior visible. Stage a friendly agent tournament on a simple task, such as sorting a messy backlog, and read the logs together to see which strategy won.

items.title: Easter Gay Maanao: AdLabs plus Claude produces an audit and executive report in 10 minutes
items.summary: An Amazon ads specialist reports that AdLabs paired with Claude generates a full audit and executive report in about 10 minutes, a job she says takes more than an hour by hand. The post has 1 reaction.
items.author: Easter Gay Maanao
items.enterprise_translation: Time each report you produce weekly, then rebuild the slowest one with an assistant connected to the source data. A before and after stopwatch number sells the idea better than a demo.

items.title: Helium 10 MCP lets Ads users create keyword harvesting and negative targeting rules by prompt
items.summary: Helium 10 says its MCP connection now builds and applies keyword harvesting and negative targeting rules across multiple campaigns from plain-language prompts. The post has 6 reactions and 2 comments.
items.author: Helium 10 (H10bradley)
items.enterprise_translation: Rules written in sentences instead of settings screens widen who can run them. Try describing one routine campaign tweak in a single sentence to your tool's assistant and compare the result to doing it by hand.

sections.title: TikTok
sections.description: Platform and creator signals from TikTok. Video-level view counts were not available to us this week.

items.title: TikTok Business App Center opens an Agentic Hub with 156 AI Skills and 2 MCP servers
items.summary: The Agentic Hub lists 156 AI skills and 2 MCP connections for advertisers, including a Seedance 2.0 skill that rewrites a proven reference ad into a new product video from a single product image. One skill was built through a conversational Claude Code workflow. The page is a live directory, so its publish date is approximate (cached 2026-10-20).
items.author: TikTok
items.enterprise_translation: A shared marketplace of installable skills lets the best workflow spread without anyone writing code. Keep a folder of your three most-reused prompts as skills and offer them to one neighboring group.

items.title: Thai creator posts 50 ChatGPT side-income ideas grouped by service, content and product sales
items.summary: A TikTok post titled '50 easy ways to make money with ChatGPT' sorts ideas into direct services, content creation and product sales. TikTok did not expose view or like counts to our fetch, so no engagement is recorded; the video ID dates the post to October 23.
items.author: @smilestory13_
items.enterprise_translation: Side-income idea lists show what a mass audience thinks AI is for. Skim ten comments on any such post for the jobs people want done, and mine them for internal tool ideas.

sections.title: Instagram
sections.description: Reels and posts from AI explainers on Instagram, with likes and comments as shown on each page.

items.title: Hindi-language creator explains Claude Duet to a new audience
items.summary: @techplus.ai walks a Hindi-speaking audience through Duet as an assistant that spots important tasks and suggests them before being asked. The Reel has 795 likes and 17 comments.
items.author: @techplus.ai
items.enterprise_translation: Local-language explainers reach audiences that English launch posts miss. Translate your best internal how-to into the language of your largest regional site and see who opens it.

items.title: Comment-keyword funnel: a creator offers a Claude readiness checklist for Duet
items.summary: @nostro_ai offers a checklist to get Claude ready before Duet arrives, delivered when viewers comment the word DUET. The Reel has 30 likes and 6 comments.
items.author: @nostro_ai
items.enterprise_translation: A keyword in the comments turns a post into a lead list. Offer a one-page template on your next internal announcement and have people reply with a keyword to receive it.

items.title: @worldof.aix pitches Duet as an assistant that works without being prompted
items.summary: The Reel presents Claude Duet as assistance that works proactively instead of waiting for prompts and invites viewers to comment 'Duet' for a link. It has 124 likes and 21 comments.
items.author: @worldof.aix
items.enterprise_translation: Short demos with one clear promise travel. Script a 20-second clip of a single task your assistant did without being asked and share it as the first slide of your next update.

items.title: Explainer Reel on Citrini Research's move into AI drug discovery
items.summary: @notinyourcurriculum explains that Citrini Research, an investment firm, looked past crowded AI infrastructure to healthcare and, in place of its usual expert calls, worked with Anthropic on protein-binder design. The post has 5 likes and 1 comment.
items.author: @notinyourcurriculum
items.enterprise_translation: Outsiders can frame the problem and let a model do the specialist work. Ask a scientist to name a problem they find neglected, and spend an afternoon having an assistant draft the first approach.

sections.title: Facebook
sections.description: Facebook and Meta community tooling this week.

items.title: Forum adds admin AI that tags pending posts against group rules and drafts posts for admins
items.summary: Meta's Forum app for Facebook Groups now has admin AI that tags pending posts as likely meeting or breaking group rules, drafts posts for admins to publish, and a more flexible Admin Assist that combines conditions like post length and link use. Co-admins also get a shared content calendar. Available in the US on iOS and Android.
items.author: Meta
items.enterprise_translation: Rule-aware triage turns a queue into a list of decisions. Point an assistant at your own review queue, such as ideas, requests or tickets, with the criteria written out, and have it pre-sort the pile each morning.

sections.title: Creator and Consumer Platforms
sections.description: YouTube and Pinterest signals showing how creators and consumers use generative AI.

items.title: YouTube study: 72% of video posters aged 14 to 44 use AI and 61% want to insert themselves
items.summary: YouTube's Culture & Trends report 'Human Creativity and AI', run with NRG among U.S. people aged 14 to 44, finds 72% of video posters use AI on videos or images and 61% are interested in using AI to put themselves into their content.
items.author: YouTube Culture & Trends
items.enterprise_translation: People want AI to put them in the picture, not replace them. Test a personal avatar or voice clone for your internal explainer videos and see whether view-through rises compared with a faceless version.

items.title: Pinterest and Barbie launch DreamHouse styles in Restyle for reimagining your own room
items.summary: Pinterest's Restyle tool lets people upload a room photo and apply five Barbie DreamHouse styles in seconds (mid-century Americana, chalet chic, superstar glam, Victorian romance, modern coastal), then swap in shoppable decor.
items.author: Pinterest / Mattel
items.enterprise_translation: Upload a photo, pick a style, see it in your own space. Offer a try-it-in-your-room flow for your own surfaces or finishes, using a photo and five named styles.

sections.title: AI for Science
sections.description: Scientist-facing AI stories surfaced this week (the scorpion-toxin binder run is in Top Picks).

items.title: KRICT lets researchers steer self-driving labs in plain language, cutting searches from about 30 to under 10
items.summary: Korea Research Institute of Chemical Technology built a framework where an LLM turns a researcher's statement like 'increasing the temperature improves yield' into priors for Bayesian optimization, with a detector that switches off advice the data contradicts. In tests on real-data simulations, one reaction needed fewer than 10 searches instead of about 30, and a conductive composite needed 3 to 5 instead of about 20. Published in the Journal of Chemical Information and Modeling; a Co-Scientist chat interface is released.
items.author: KRICT (Dr. Gwang-Noh Ahn)
items.enterprise_translation: Scientists keep their intuition in the loop by just saying it. Give a skeptical lab a chat box where hunches become inputs to the next experiment, and run one parameter sweep with and without their guidance.
items.why_it_matters: Off-platform item kept because social-platform AI-for-science posts about lab automation were thin this week.

items.summary: Mentioned in 11 sampled items: 10 Instagram Reels and one LinkedIn post by Allie K. Miller.
items.author: Social tab
items.enterprise_translation: Watch which launch gets same-day creator explainers; those are the ones worth a 20-minute test. Join the waitlist and run a morning-brief experiment.

items.title: Meta Muse
items.summary: Mentioned in 4 sampled items: two Allie K. Miller posts, one e-commerce digest and Meta's earnings call.
items.author: Social tab
items.enterprise_translation: A tool that keeps showing up across unrelated feeds is worth a hands-on hour. Ask it to plan a small trip or a purchase and compare to your usual search.
items.recurrence_note: Muse was the top tool in last week's tally.

items.title: Claude Science
items.summary: Mentioned in 5 sampled Instagram posts on the scorpion-toxin binder run, including Anthropic's own.
items.author: Social tab
items.enterprise_translation: Watch for the first lab in your orbit that reports a bench result from a model-designed candidate and borrow their protocol.

items.title: OpenAI dots
items.summary: Mentioned in 3 sampled items: two Allie K. Miller posts and one Duet explainer Reel.
items.author: Social tab
items.enterprise_translation: Dots is pitched at people who code and live in Slack; test it on one chat-heavy workflow for a day.

items.title: Instinct
items.summary: Mentioned in 2 sampled Allie K. Miller posts as the iMessage-native agent that can watch the internet for you.
items.author: Social tab
items.enterprise_translation: Try the watchdog idea: ask any agent to message you whenever a named writer, competitor or standard publishes something new.

items.title: MCP connections to ads and sales data
items.summary: Mentioned in 4 sampled LinkedIn posts: Helium 10 MCP, Data Dive MCP (421 teams connected in six weeks, per its post), AdLabs plus Claude, and Bailiff's weekly report.
items.author: Social tab
items.enterprise_translation: Connect one data source your weekly report depends on to an assistant over MCP and let it write the first draft.

items.title: ChatGPT shopping plugins
items.summary: Mentioned in 2 sampled items: the Ulta Beauty AI Bundles plugin and a Thai TikTok post of ChatGPT side-income ideas.
items.author: Social tab
items.enterprise_translation: Sketch what a plugin for your own catalog would answer in its first five conversations.

items.title: Pinterest Restyle
items.summary: Mentioned in 2 sampled items: the Barbie DreamHouse launch coverage in LBB and Social Media Today.
items.author: Social tab
items.enterprise_translation: Photo-in, style-out is a flow people understand instantly; try it with your own product photos.

emerging_signals.pattern: Comment-keyword delivery is the standard Instagram AI funnel
emerging_signals.evidence: Three of the Duet Reels sampled (@nostro_ai, @tarunonsi, @worldof.aix) offer a checklist, guide or link when viewers comment a keyword.
emerging_signals.what_to_watch: Whether the same pattern shows up in LinkedIn comment sections next week.

emerging_signals.evidence: Allie K. Miller's three-rules post (281 reactions, 199 comments) and Bailiff's style file both treat a written document about you as the main input to an assistant.
emerging_signals.what_to_watch: Template swaps of urgency lists and style files.

emerging_signals.pattern: Nonexpert groups driving AI science runs
emerging_signals.evidence: Anthropic says the scorpion-toxin project was steered by Citrini Research, an investment research firm, with four follow-up prompts over 64 hours.
emerging_signals.what_to_watch: The next domain where an outside group posts lab-validated results.

suggested_refinements.notes: Platform access limits this week: TikTok video pages did not expose view, like or comment counts to our fetch, so the TikTok section has two items and no engagement numbers (the Agentic Hub is a live directory, so its date is approximate). Facebook video pages did not expose publish dates or counts, so none were promoted; Facebook coverage rests on the Meta newsroom. Threads profile pages returned cached text without reliable counts, so the Threads item sits in the index only. The creator watch list accounts (@rpn, @nocode.joshua and others) could not be read for the window. Instagram engagement and LinkedIn reactions were read from the live pages on 2026-10-25 and will have grown since. Instagram dates come from the page caption date; LinkedIn dates come from the post timestamp converted to Pacific time. The AI-for-science item comes from a press release rather than a social post.
